key_insight: Machine learning on EHR data can accurately infer several family relationship types, including parent-child, sibling, twin, and partner links.
clinical_relevance: Automatically identifying family ties could strengthen patient-centered research and improve context-aware healthcare applications by linking related records at scale.
method: Used Random Forest classifiers to predict five relationship types: mother-child, father-child, sibling-sibling, twin-twin, and partner-partner.
Built and refined models in four stages: initial training, multicollinearity reduction, feature engineering, and training-data restriction to linkable pairs.
Compared large Indiana EHR data (INPC) against natality birth certificate records as the gold standard.
evidence_signal: Across relationship types, models achieved precision of 0.92-1.00, recall of 0.97-1.00, and F1 scores of 0.94-1.00, with high-confidence predictions capturing 77-99% of true positives.
watch_item: A substantial share of verified relationships had no shared contact information in the EHR, limiting detectability and potentially reducing real-world coverage.
paper_title: Identifying Family Relationships from Electronic Health Records: A Machine Learning Approach
